title: Etale base change covers the fibre component through a lifted point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $r:Z\to S$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $P=X\times_S Z$ with projections $p:P\to X$ and $g:P\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix $z\in Z$ and $a\in P$ with $g(a)=z$. If $C_a$ is the connected component of $a$ in $g^{-1}(z)$ and $C_{p(a)}$ is the connected component of $p(a)$ in $f^{-1}(r(z))$, then $C_{p(a)}\subseteq p(C_a)$. Here a connected component means the maximal connected subset containing the indicated point [def-weil-connected-scheme], in the subspace topology on the indicated fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

lean.statement:
theorem connectedComponentIn_subset_image_pullback_fst {X S Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (r : Z ⟶ S) [Etale r] {z : Z} (p : ↑(pullback f r))
    (hp : pullback.snd f r p = z) :
    connectedComponentIn (f ⁻¹' {r z}) (pullback.fst f r p) ⊆
      pullback.fst f r '' connectedComponentIn (pullback.snd f r ⁻¹' {z}) p
lean.note: The source declaration has exactly the node statement: for a locally finite type f and étale r, and p over z in the pullback, the connected component in the f-fibre is contained in the image under pullback.fst of the connected component in the pullback fibre.
